newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end up on funds, program buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end up on funds, program buying.

text.p: A combination of local funds and foreign program buying lifted Kuala Lumpur blue chips above the 1,100 level ahead of a Moslem holiday on Thursday.
At the closing bell, the Composite Index of 100 leading stocks closed up 17.14 points or 1.57 percent to 1,107.14. It hit a 1,110.43 session high earlier.

"We heard it could be foreign program buying on selective index-linked heavyweights especially the banks," said Patrick Zecha, head of research at South Johor Securities. He said that while the gain was encouraging, "it's not broad-based", with other indicators such as the Second Board index flat.
